Both captures describe separate eligibility for receiving Link via Connect and controlling Link settings. Connected accounts can manage their own settings if the platform uses direct charges, creates and charges payment methods on connected accounts, and the accounts have full Dashboard access. Cloned platform payment methods, destination charges, separate charges and transfers, or absence of full Dashboard access leave control with the platform. Distinguish payments through the platform from payments processed without it. `disableLink` can selectively disable for specific accounts where the platform controls settings (old raw lines 65-107, new raw lines 66-108). The general automatic availability sentence does not displace the separate granted-access/India qualifications or guarantee per-session production display.

Source lines 13-17 use technical-sounding Card Element deprecation where the paired guides give recommendation wording. Keep the existing reciprocal Link route and distinguish the Payment Request Button limitation and conditional earlier compatibility.

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-link-card-element-link-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-card-element-link-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-card-element-link.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/card-element-link`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: The November 7 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/card-element-link describes Link sign-up, verification and autofill with single-line and split Card Elements. New Link users are asked for an email address, phone number and payment method. They can also enter their card in the Card Element first and then save it to a Link account (old raw lines 23-28 and 37-43, new raw lines 24-29 and 38-44). Returning customers may be asked for SMS or email verification and the guide describes a 90-day authentication window. An enabled Card Element can show Link to granted-access accounts, with an India exclusion, browser pop-up support, opener communication and typically 350 by 28 pixel container guidance. An eligible sandbox displays Link when enabled and production may vary. The guide says to keep real user data out of sandbox Link accounts because those accounts are associated with the publishable key (old raw lines 109-119 and new raw lines 110-120). Dashboard disablement and disableLink are separate controls. For Connect, direct charges, creating and charging payment methods on connected accounts and full Dashboard access permit account settings control. Otherwise the platform controls platform payments in the listed cases (old raw lines 14-59, old raw lines 65-128, new raw lines 15-60 and new raw lines 66-129). source-stripe-card-element-link.md captures much of the May behavior. November instead recommends Contact Details Element alongside Express Checkout Element and Payment Element and explicitly excludes the separate Payment Request Button from Endive or later (old raw lines 6-12, old raw lines 61-63, new raw lines 7-13 and new raw lines 62-64). Link sign-up, successful verification or display does not prove completed payment.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/card-element-link, The Card Element captures establish a change in the displayed name and recommendation link, with Express Checkout Element and Payment Element retained (old raw lines 6-12,130-134, new raw lines 7-13,131-135). The separate May 27 Dahlia changelog identifies Contact Details Element as the renamed Link Authentication Element. It documents unchanged contact collection and Link authentication for these Web Elements flows and supports both `elements.create('linkAuthentication')` and `elements.create('contactDetails')` without an existing-integration change. The two Contact Details guides corroborate the renamed identity (raw/stripe-changelog-dahlia-2026-05-27-link-authentication-element-rename-2026-11-07.md:5-13, raw/stripe-payments-link-contact-details-element-2026-11-07.md:5-13, raw/stripe-payments-elements-contact-details-element-2026-11-07.md:5-11). Preserve May terminology as dated in the reciprocal Link concept. The alias evidence applies to these Web Elements creation calls. The paired Card Element guides retain the Card Element flow for existing integrations and describe it as no longer recommended. The separate Payment Request Button is deprecated and unsupported in Stripe.js Endive or later. Both Link surfaces can still appear independently on an earlier supported version of Stripe.js (old raw lines 61-63 and new raw lines 62-64). Scope the version warning and conditional coexistence reciprocally in Stripe Link and its separate Payment Request Button route. source-stripe-card-element-link.md should preserve May provenance and earlier advice as dated. Changes to screenshot links, formatting, numbering and table spacing are presentation, with no new Connect, browser or sandbox behavior (old raw lines 18-29, old raw lines 65-128, new raw lines 19-30 and new raw lines 66-129). Keep eligibility separate from selective production visibility, typical size guidance from absolute thresholds, and authentication and autofill from a live payment outcome. The November SDK boundary concerns the Button Element and does not establish removal of the lower-level paymentRequest API.
